does: Sets a mix of beaten egg and soft cooked potato in a small pan into a thick, round cake, golden outside and tender or even creamy in the middle. It is turned over once with the help of a plate.

intro.what: Egg and softened potato form a thick Spanish tortilla that is turned with a plate.
intro.why: Gentle heat and a coherent underside let you manage a substantial egg cake without tearing it during the turn.

how: Heat a spoonful of the kept oil in a small non-stick pan over a medium heat, so that it coats the base and the sides.
Pour in the mix of egg and potato and press it level. It should hiss softly, not spit.
Cook gently. Shake the pan now and then and run a spatula round the edge to keep it neat and tucked in, until the underside is golden and the edge has set while the top is still wet.
Turn it over onto a flat plate and slide it back, as in the flip, then tuck the edges in and cook the other side briefly.
Slide it onto a plate and let it stand a while. The middle can be left soft or set firm, as the cook likes.

cues.text: The edge pulls from the pan and turns pale gold, and the top shrinks from wet to a soft, glossy skin.
The pan shakes freely and the cake slides on the oil.
A sweet, eggy smell. A sharp, burnt smell means the heat is too high.

mistakes.mistake: Cooking it too hot, so that the outside burns before the egg in the middle has begun to set.
mistakes.fix: Cook it over a medium heat or lower, and give it time.

mistakes.mistake: Turning it before the underside has set, so that it tears and runs.
mistakes.fix: Wait until the edge is firm and the cake slides when the pan is shaken.

mistakes.mistake: Using a pan far too big, which leaves a thin, dry cake.
mistakes.fix: Use a small, deep pan, so that the cake is thick.

quiz.question: Why use a suitably small pan for this tortilla?
choices: To spread the mixture as thinly as possible.
To keep a thick cake rather than a thin dry layer.
To make the egg set as a very thin outer film.
quiz.because: Pan size controls the depth and texture of the tortilla.

quiz.question: What should you check before the plate-assisted turn?
choices: The underside is still loose and runs freely.
The cake is stuck firmly to the base.
The edge is firm and the cake slides when shaken.
quiz.because: A coherent moving cake is easier to turn without tearing.

quiz.question: What pan movement suggests the tortilla is released?
choices: The cake slides freely when the pan is shaken.
The pan moves but the cake stays fixed.
Only loose egg moves around a stuck base.
quiz.because: Sliding shows that the cake can move as a joined shape before the turn.

quiz.question: The outside scorches before the centre starts setting. What should change?
choices: Raise the heat to darken the surface faster.
Lower the heat for gentler cooking.
Keep the heat high but turn the cake repeatedly.
quiz.because: Gentler heat gives the thicker mixture time to change without burning the exterior.

comes_after.why: The potato has to be soft before the egg goes round it, and it is cooked soft in oil first.
The cake is turned over in the same way as any food that must be turned while its top is still soft.

variant_of.differs: The egg is a thick flat cake with soft potato inside it and is never rolled. It is cooked slowly, turned over with a plate, and served warm or at room temperature, with the middle left soft or firm to taste. A rolled omelette is thin, quick and creamy.
